efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. The mouse allergic contact dermatitis model is named in the full text (checker-confirmed; web-search snippet) but not in the abstract. First use proxied by the Phase 2 start (Dec 2009).
efficacy.note: LEO 29102 went into patients on a mouse topical allergic contact dermatitis model, with dose-dependent skin TNF-alpha inhibition.
efficacy.quote: This effort culminated in identification of LEO 29102 (20), a potent, selective, and soft-drug PDE4 inhibitor with properties suitable for patient-friendly formulations giving efficient drug delivery to the skin.
efficacy.judgement: Separate system from crisaborole's phorbol-ester ear edema: a hapten allergic model used by LEO for its own candidate.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: EASI change vs vehicle: -2.86 best LEO 29102 dose vs -0.85 vehicle, p=0.08; no dose significant
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results (NCT01037881) read directly; model side abstract-level. The sponsor paper called the Phase 2 efficacy 'clinically relevant' without reporting the primary endpoint.
efficacy.note: Phase 2 primary endpoint (EASI change at day 28) was not significant versus vehicle at any of five LEO 29102 strengths.
efficacy.short: Phase 2 primary missed at every dose
efficacy.quote: Absolute Change in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) Score From Baseline (Last Observation Carried Forward [LOCF])
efficacy.judgement: Pairing: the registry's ANOVA p-values (0.27, 0.83, 0.08, 0.16, 0.14) set the status, not the sponsor's 2014 'clinically relevant efficacy' claim, which gave no primary-endpoint result (rule 7: the 2014 claim is not an admissible comparison). Active control pimecrolimus separated (p=0.04), so the trial could detect an effect.

efficacy.confidence_note: Study date not given in the review; 2012 is a proxy (first Phase 2, NCT01702181, started Aug 2012).
efficacy.note: Difamilast's filed efficacy model was a mouse chronic contact dermatitis; it outperformed crisaborole there.
efficacy.quote: Difamilast showed efficacy in a mouse model of chronic contact dermatitis.
efficacy.judgement: Separate from LEO's acute allergic model: repeated hapten challenges, Otsuka protocol.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse dermatitis score reduction vs IGA success over vehicle in Phase 2/3
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Patient side: Hanifin 2016 (doi:10.1016/j.jaad.2016.04.001, primary IGA met at week 4, P=.0165), Saeki 2019 and the 2021 Phase 3 trials, all met their primaries.
efficacy.note: Otsuka set the mouse result beside difamilast's clinical efficacy: the model agreed with positive Phase 2 and 3 trials.
efficacy.quote: Difamilast, a novel selective phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) inhibitor, demonstrated significant efficacy without adverse reactions such as nausea and diarrhea in patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) and was recently approved in Japan.
efficacy.judgement: Dated 2023, when the model data were first public beside the trials. Scored prospective, not retro, because the FDA review files it as the primary pharmacology model; the paper's crisaborole comparator arm may be later, which I could not date.

added_models.model: Human skin explants: dermal open-flow microperfusion with tissue cAMP

efficacy.model: Human skin explants: dermal open-flow microperfusion with tissue cAMP
efficacy.note: LEO built a barrier-impaired human skin explant readout (free drug in dermal fluid, tissue cAMP) to explain clinical outcomes of its topical PDE4 inhibitors.
efficacy.quote: To investigate the difference in clinical efficacy in AD patients between two topical PDE4 inhibitors using dermal open flow microperfusion and cAMP as a pharmacodynamic read-out in fresh human skin explants.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use, which came after both trials.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: explant target engagement (cAMP raised, dISF 2100 nM) vs LEO 29102 Phase 2 primary EASI endpoint not met
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The paper treats LEO 29102 as clinically efficacious against LEO 39652 (not a class member); the registry primary endpoint for LEO 29102 was not significant.
efficacy.model: Human skin explants: dermal open-flow microperfusion with tissue cAMP
efficacy.note: Explants showed LEO 29102 engaged PDE4 in barrier-impaired skin, implying efficacy, but its Phase 2 primary endpoint failed.
efficacy.quote: Elevated cAMP levels were observed with LEO 29102 while no evidence of target engagement was obtained with LEO 39652.
efficacy.judgement: A retrodiction. The authors call it a match because they read LEO 29102 as clinically active. Against the registry primary (no dose significant, best p=0.08) it fails to reproduce the result, so contra. A near-miss trend could make this arguable; low confidence.

efficacy.note: Academic group tested difamilast in oxazolone-induced allergic skin inflammation, a common mouse model of atopic dermatitis.
efficacy.quote: In this study, we addressed this unsolved issue by analyzing the action of difamilast, a novel phosphodiesterase 4 inhibitor, on an oxazolone-induced skin allergic inflammation commonly used as a mouse model of atopic dermatitis.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse ear inflammation reduction vs approved clinical efficacy
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Calama 2024 (doi:10.1111/exd.70024) reproduced crisaborole efficacy in a 4-challenge oxazolone model, calling it 'responsive to AD standard of care therapies in humans'.
efficacy.note: Difamilast reduced oxazolone skin inflammation, reproducing the approved clinical effect; crisaborole did the same in Almirall's version (2024).
efficacy.quote: Topical application of difamilast ameliorated skin inflammation in association with reduced IL-4 expression even when the treatment commenced 4 days after the initiation of oxazolone challenge, showing its therapeutic effect on atopic dermatitis.
efficacy.judgement: Takahashi (difamilast) and Calama (crisaborole) treated as one system: repeated oxazolone challenge on mouse ear. Earliest public comparison sets the year.

efficacy.note: Otsuka tested difamilast in MC903-induced AD mice for itch, ear thickness and barrier loss, after clinical approval.
efficacy.quote: Therefore, we evaluated the effects of difamilast on pruritus, dermatitis, and skin barrier dysfunction in MC903-induced AD model mice.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: scratching, ear thickness and TEWL reduction vs clinical IGA/itch response
efficacy.note: Difamilast cut scratching, ear swelling and water loss in MC903 mice, reproducing its known clinical effect.
efficacy.quote: One of the topical PDE4 inhibitors, difamilast, has been shown to be effective in the clinical treatment of AD.
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison: the paper opens on clinical efficacy and reproduces it in mice; retro since run after the trials.

considered_not_added: Difamilast PBMC TNF-alpha release (Hiyama 2023): same system as the draft's pbmc-cytokine-release track.
Difamilast minipig/rat dermal toxicity and PK (FDA 219474 review; Hiyama 2023): same system as the draft's minipig-dermal-tox track.

Difamilast PDE4B-over-PDE4D selectivity as a predictor of no nausea/emesis (Hiyama 2023): a recombinant-enzyme rationale; low systemic exposure explains the absence equally, and no source compares the selectivity prediction itself with patients.
Calama 2024 four-challenge oxazolone model with crisaborole: folded into mouse-oxazolone-dermatitis (same system), cited in its confidence_note.
Youn 2023 crisaborole in psoriasis-like, filaggrin-deficient AD-like and S. aureus mouse models: no patient comparison (authors say translation needs further examination).
Eirefelt 2020 explant for LEO 39652: not a class member; only the LEO 29102 arm scored.
DRM02: Phase 2 failure from Dermira 10-K (tier 5), but no model side found; nothing to add as a track.
AN2898: Phase 2 NCT01301508 with no posted results found and no published model side.
Patient-derived cells / organoids, human genetic and QSP dose models: none found for topical PDE4 inhibitors in AD.
